activity_context.topic_title: The Arc Length of a Planar Curve

feedback.problem: The length of the curve $y=\sqrt[3]{x}$ on $[1,9]$ is given by
feedback.worked_solution:
The arc length of a curve $y=f(x)$ between $x=1$ and $x=9$ can be found using the formula

$$
L={\int }_{a}^{b}\sqrt{1+[{f}^{′}(x)]^{2}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $f(x)=\sqrt[3]{x},$ $a=1,$ and $b=9.$

First, we find the derivative of $f(x):$

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=\frac{1}{3\sqrt[3]{{x}^{2}}}
$$

Substituting ${f}^{′}(x)=\frac{1}{3\sqrt[3]{{x}^{2}}}$ into the arc length formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{1}^{9}\sqrt{1+[{f}^{′}(x)]^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{9}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{1}{3\sqrt[3]{{x}^{2}}})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{9}\sqrt{1+\frac{1}{9x\sqrt[3]{x}}}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$
